examples.en: This glutinous rice cake is really chewy and sticky.
If the dough is sticky, it clings to your hands.
I like sticky rice.
The rice cake was stickier than I expected.
I want to eat sticky, chewy rice cake.

examples.ko: 쌀을 바꿨더니 밥이 더 차져서 맛있어요.
examples.en: After changing the rice, the cooked rice got stickier and tastier.

explain: 밥, 떡, 반죽처럼 끈기가 있어서 달라붙는 느낌일 때 써요. 비슷한 '쫄깃하다'는 씹는 맛이 탄력 있다는 쪽이라 차지다와 같이 쓰는 경우가 많아요. '차진 밥'처럼 -ㄴ으로 꾸미는 형태를 자주 써요.
explain_en: Used for food like rice, rice cake, or dough that has a sticky, clingy texture. 쫄깃하다 focuses on the bouncy chew, and the two often appear together. The modifier form '차진' (as in 차진 밥) is very common.

en: be carried out; be performed; be executed

examples.en: The work is carried out as planned.

examples.ko: 이 일은 팀 전체의 협력으로 수행되어야 해요.
examples.en: This task has to be carried out through the whole team's cooperation.
The mission was carried out safely.

examples.ko: 검사가 하루에 두 번 수행되는 곳이에요.
examples.en: It's a place where inspections are carried out twice a day.
What was promised wasn't carried out properly.
All the procedures will be carried out in order.

explain: 일이나 임무가 주어가 되어 이루어진다는 느낌이라 사람이 하는 '수행하다'와 짝이에요. 주로 업무, 임무, 검사처럼 격식 있는 글과 말에서 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '하다/되다'로 풀어서 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: This is the passive partner of 수행하다: the task or mission is the subject, and it just gets done. It sounds formal and fits work, missions, and inspections. In casual talk Koreans often say simpler things like 하다 or 되다 instead.

examples.en: I was left off this list.
Children are excluded from the discount.
That item was dropped from the meeting agenda.
The injured player will be left out of the game.
Please make sure nobody is left out.

examples.ko: 저만 계획에서 제외된 것 같아서 서운해요.
examples.en: I feel hurt because it seems only I was left out of the plan.

explain: '에서'와 함께 '명단에서 제외되다'처럼 어디서 빠졌는지를 같이 말해요. 사람이 빠지면 기분이 상하는 느낌이 있고, 안내문에서는 명사 '제외'만 써서 '○○ 제외'라고도 해요. 반대말은 '포함되다'예요.
explain_en: Pair it with 에서 to say what you were dropped from, like 명단에서 제외되다. When a person is the one left out it can carry a hurt feeling. On notices you will also see the bare noun, like '○○ 제외'. The opposite is 포함되다.

examples.en: I reread the report and revised it.
Please correct the wrong parts.
How about revising the plan a little?
I touched up the photo's colors and then posted it.

examples.ko: 한 번 보낸 글은 수정할 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't edit a post once it's sent.
I wrote the name wrong, so I came to fix it.

explain: 글, 계획, 사진처럼 이미 있는 것을 조금 고칠 때 써요. '고치다'는 고장 난 물건에도 쓰지만 수정하다는 문서나 내용에 더 잘 어울려요. '바로잡다'는 틀린 것을 맞게 한다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: Use it for adjusting something that already exists, such as a text, plan, or photo. 고치다 also covers fixing broken objects, but 수정하다 fits documents and content better. 바로잡다 leans more toward making a mistake right.

examples.en: Submission of this document is requested by tomorrow.
If help is requested, I'll go right away.
Attendance at the meeting was requested.
It's a situation where cooperation is requested.
Additional materials may be requested.

examples.ko: 요청된 일은 오늘 안에 끝내야 해요.
examples.en: The requested work has to be finished today.

explain: '~이/가 요청되다'는 주어가 요청받는 일이라서 누가 요청했는지는 말하지 않아요. 안내문, 공문, 뉴스에서 자주 보이고 일상 대화에서는 '부탁받다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: The subject is the thing being asked for, and who asked is left unsaid. You see it in notices, official letters, and news. In everyday talk people prefer simpler phrasing such as 부탁받다.

examples.en: This product was certified as safe.
When the account is verified, you get a text message.
Only verified shops appear in the app.
You get verified only after your identity is confirmed.
It's a site that hasn't been verified yet.
I'll wait until it's certified by an official body.

explain: 제품, 계정, 가게가 믿을 만하다고 확인받았을 때 써요. 앱이나 사이트에서 '인증 완료', '인증 번호'처럼 아주 자주 보여요. 사람의 실력을 인정받을 때는 '인정되다'를 써요.
explain_en: Used when a product, account, or shop is officially confirmed as trustworthy. You see it constantly in apps, like 인증 완료 or 인증 번호. For a person's ability being recognized, use 인정되다 instead.

en: be traded; be bought and sold

examples.ko: 이 책은 중고 시장에서 비싸게 거래돼요.
examples.en: This book sells for a high price on the used market.
That painting sold for 100 million won.
The stock is being actively traded.
Don't buy items that are traded illegally.
I wonder how much the house will go for.

examples.ko: 거래된 내역은 앱에서 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see the transaction history in the app.

explain: 물건이나 주식이 사고팔리는 상태를 말해요. 사람이 주어이면 '거래하다'를 써요. '중고 거래', '직거래'처럼 명사 '거래'로 훨씬 자주 쓰고, '억 원에 거래되다'처럼 '에'로 가격을 붙여요.
explain_en: It describes goods or stocks being bought and sold. If a person is the subject, use 거래하다 instead. The noun 거래 is much more common, as in 중고 거래 and 직거래, and you add the price with 에, like 억 원에 거래되다.

examples.ko: 이 개는 잘 훈련돼서 말을 잘 들어요.
examples.en: This dog is well trained, so it listens well.
The players are trained hard every day.
A trained staff member will guide you.
It's dangerous if you aren't trained enough.
Once your body is trained, it's less tiring.
The soldiers were trained strictly.

explain: 사람이나 동물이 훈련을 받아 몸에 익은 상태예요. 스스로 연습하는 것은 '훈련하다', 시켜서 하게 하는 것은 '훈련시키다'로 나눠요. '훈련된 개'처럼 꾸미는 말로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It describes a person or animal that has gone through training and has the skill. Doing it yourself is 훈련하다, and making someone else do it is 훈련시키다. It often shows up as a modifier, like 훈련된 개.

examples.en: I train my puppy every day.
The coach trained the players hard.
I've been put in charge of training the new hires.
I'm training my child to sleep alone.
Training a horse takes a long time.
We trained the staff and sent them out to the site.

explain: '~을 훈련시키다'는 내가 직접 하지 않고 대상이 훈련하게 만드는 말이에요. 내가 몸으로 연습하면 '훈련하다'예요. 같은 뜻으로 '훈련을 시키다'로 띄어 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: ~을 훈련시키다 means you make someone or something else go through training instead of doing it yourself. If you practice yourself, it is 훈련하다. You can also split it as 훈련을 시키다 with the same meaning.

examples.en: I belong to the sales team.
Which team did that player belong to?
It's a research institute affiliated with a university.
Where are you affiliated now?
If you belong to a company, you get insurance.
I'm anxious because I don't belong to anywhere yet.

explain: '~에 소속하다'는 조직에 속해 있다는 뜻인데, 말할 때는 '~에 속해 있다'나 '~ 소속이다'를 더 많이 써요. 소개할 때도 '○○ 소속이에요'처럼 명사로 써요. 소속하다는 글이나 공식적인 말에 가까워요.
explain_en: The pattern is ~에 소속하다, but in speech people more often say ~에 속해 있다 or ~ 소속이다. When introducing yourself you use the noun, like '○○ 소속이에요'. The verb itself sounds written or official.

examples.en: This rule applies to all students.
The discount hasn't been applied yet.
The new law takes effect from next month.
It's the price with the coupon applied.
There are cases where exceptions apply.

examples.ko: 배운 내용이 실생활에 적용될 때 재미있어요.
examples.en: It's fun when what you learned is applied to real life.

explain: 규칙, 할인, 설정이 어떤 대상에 실제로 닿을 때 써요. '학생에게 적용되다'처럼 누구에게 해당하는지를 같이 말해요. '적용하다'는 사람이 그것을 쓰는 것이고, 적용되다는 그것이 저절로 걸리는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Use it when a rule, discount, or setting actually reaches something. Say who it covers with 에게, like 학생에게 적용되다. 적용하다 is when a person uses it; 적용되다 feels like it kicks in on its own.

examples.en: This street is designated as a no-smoking zone.
My seat has already been assigned.
Please come at the designated time.
That building was designated a cultural heritage site.
I'll let you know once a person in charge is assigned.

examples.ko: 주차는 지정되어 있는 곳에만 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only park in designated spots.

explain: 사람이 아니라 장소, 시간, 자리가 주어로 '정해진다'는 뜻이에요. '지정석'(정해진 자리), '지정 장소'처럼 명사 앞에 붙는 경우가 많아요. 그냥 '정해지다'보다 공식적으로 정해졌다는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: The subject is a place, time, or seat that gets officially set. It often attaches to nouns, as in 지정석 (assigned seat) and 지정 장소. Compared with the plain 정해지다, it sounds more official.

examples.en: Grandfather cuts the grass with a sickle.
A sickle has a sharp blade, so you must be careful.

examples.ko: 농사를 짓는 분들은 낫을 자주 써요.
examples.en: People who farm often use sickles.
A sickle hangs in the storage shed of the country house.
I bought a new sickle.

examples.ko: 벼를 낫으로 베던 시절 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard a story about the days when rice was cut with sickles.

explain: 풀이나 곡식을 베는, 끝이 굽은 농기구예요. 소리가 같은 '낫다'(병이 나아지다, 더 좋다)와 헷갈리지 않게 문장 속 쓰임을 봐야 해요. 낫은 '낫이, 낫을, 낫으로'처럼 받침 ㅅ이 다음 소리로 넘어가요.
explain_en: It's the farm tool with a curved blade for cutting grass or grain. Don't confuse it with the verb 낫다 (to get better, to be better), which sounds the same; context tells them apart. With particles the ㅅ carries over, as in 낫이, 낫을, 낫으로.

examples.en: A staff member led me to the meeting room.
Please show the guests to their seats.

examples.ko: 길을 모르는 사람들을 안전한 곳으로 인도해요.
examples.en: They guide people who don't know the way to a safe place.
The teacher led us down a good path.
I work guiding tourists.
If you lead the way, everyone will follow.

explain: 사람을 어디로 데리고 가서 안내한다는 뜻이고, 길을 알려 주는 '안내하다'보다 격식 있고 약간 문어적이에요. 일상에서는 '안내하다'나 '데려가다'를 더 많이 써요. 물건이나 권리를 넘겨준다는 뜻의 '인도하다(引渡)'는 소리만 같은 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It means taking someone somewhere and guiding them, and sounds more formal and bookish than 안내하다. In daily speech 안내하다 or 데려가다 is more common. 인도하다 (引渡), meaning to hand over goods or rights, is a different word that only sounds the same.

examples.en: My younger sibling has a playful expression.
That child gave a mischievous smile.
I said it playfully, but they took it seriously.
I was in a good mood today, so I felt playful.
Even though he looks playful, he's a serious friend inside.
Her voice is playful and cute.

explain: '장난'에 '-스럽다'가 붙어서 장난치는 듯한 분위기나 태도를 말해요. 진지하지 않다는 느낌이 들 수 있지만 보통은 귀엽고 밝은 쪽이에요. 심하게 짓궂으면 '짓궂다'를 써요.
explain_en: 장난 plus -스럽다 describes an attitude or mood that seems like joking around. It can suggest not being serious, but usually in a cute, light way. For truly teasing behavior, 짓궂다 is the better word.

examples.ko: 이 방은 열 명으로 인원이 제한돼요.
examples.en: The number of people in this room is limited to ten.

examples.ko: 사용 시간이 하루 한 시간으로 제한됐어요.
examples.en: Usage time was limited to one hour a day.
It's a place where entry is restricted by age.
Seats are limited, so please hurry.

examples.ko: 이 쿠폰은 한 번만 쓰도록 제한돼요.
examples.en: This coupon is limited to a single use.

examples.ko: 접근이 제한된 구역에는 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't enter areas with restricted access.

explain: 수나 시간, 범위에 한계가 정해져 있다는 뜻이고 '~로 제한되다'처럼 '로'로 한계를 말해요. 규칙을 만드는 쪽에서 막는 느낌이라 '제한하다'와 짝이에요. 반대말에 가까운 말은 '무제한'이에요.
explain_en: It means a number, time, or range has a set limit, and you state the limit with 로, like 열 명으로 제한되다. It feels like someone made a rule to restrict it, so it pairs with 제한하다. A close opposite is the noun 무제한.

examples.en: The new system will be introduced next week.
This system was introduced last year.
It's a method that was brought in from overseas.
Once self-checkout is introduced, it'll be more convenient.
I watched the process of the new technology being introduced.
It's a service that hasn't been introduced yet.

explain: 제도, 기술, 기계처럼 밖에서 들여와 쓰기 시작하는 것에 써요. 사람을 소개하는 '소개하다'와는 달라요. 보통 회사나 나라 차원의 이야기라 뉴스나 업무 대화에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: Use it for systems, technologies, or machines that are brought in from outside and begin to be used. It is different from 소개하다, which is for introducing people. It usually concerns companies or countries, so you hear it in news and work talk.

examples.en: My opinion was completely rejected, so I was upset.
That possibility hasn't been ruled out yet.
That theory was disproved by new research.

examples.ko: 노력이 부정되는 느낌이 들 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I feel as if my effort is being denied.
If the facts are denied, we need to investigate again.

examples.ko: 부정된 줄 알았던 소문이 다시 나왔어요.
examples.en: A rumor I thought had been denied came up again.

explain: 어떤 주장이나 가능성이 '아니다'로 받아들여질 때 써요. 사람이 말하는 '부정하다'와 짝이고, 주어가 의견이나 이론이에요. '부정'은 '아닌 것'이라는 뜻 말고 옳지 않은 일(부정행위)이라는 뜻의 같은 소리 말도 있어서 문장을 봐야 해요.
explain_en: Use it when a claim or possibility ends up being treated as not true. It pairs with 부정하다, and the subject is an opinion or theory. There is also a same-sounding 부정 meaning dishonest acts (부정행위), so read the context.

examples.en: I bought a drill to make a hole in the wall.

examples.ko: 드릴 소리가 너무 커서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The drill noise was so loud that I was startled.
The neighbors are working with a drill.

examples.ko: 전동 드릴은 나사를 박을 때도 편해요.
examples.en: An electric drill is also handy for driving in screws.
My father showed me how to use a drill.

examples.ko: 드릴을 쓸 때는 보안경을 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: You must wear safety glasses when using a drill.

explain: 벽이나 나무에 구멍을 뚫는 공구예요. 전기로 돌리는 것은 '전동 드릴'이라고 해요. 영어 drill에는 '반복 훈련'이라는 뜻도 있지만 한국어 드릴은 보통 공구를 가리켜요.
explain_en: This is the tool for boring holes in walls or wood; the electric kind is called 전동 드릴. English drill also means repeated practice, but in Korean 드릴 usually points to the tool.

examples.en: This sentence can be interpreted in two ways.
His words were interpreted as a refusal.
I wonder how dreams are interpreted.
The results may be interpreted differently.
It's an expression that doesn't read naturally when translated.
I corrected the content that had been misinterpreted.

explain: 말이나 글이 어떤 뜻으로 이해될 때 써요. '~로 해석되다'가 기본 틀이고, 같은 말을 사람마다 다르게 받아들일 때 자주 나와요. 다른 언어로 옮기는 것은 '번역되다'라고 해서 구분해요.
explain_en: Use it when words or writing get understood in a certain way. The basic frame is ~로 해석되다, and it often appears when people read the same thing differently. Moving it into another language is 번역되다, which is a separate word.

examples.en: Trust forms between friends.
A new culture gradually took shape.
Good habits aren't formed overnight.
This village formed along the river.
Once the mood is set, it gets easier to talk.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 형성된 성격은 잘 안 바뀌어요.
examples.en: A personality formed in childhood rarely changes.

explain: 습관, 관계, 분위기, 마을처럼 눈에 안 보이거나 시간이 걸려서 점점 만들어질 때 써요. 사람이 의도해서 하는 '만들다'와 달리 저절로 생겨나는 느낌이에요. '관계가 형성되다'처럼 추상적인 명사와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Used for things that gradually take shape over time, like habits, relationships, atmospheres, or towns. Unlike 만들다, which is intentional, it feels like something arising by itself. It goes well with abstract nouns, as in 관계가 형성되다.

examples.en: This term is defined by law.
Happiness is defined differently by each person.
Once the problem is defined exactly, it's easier to solve.

examples.ko: 처음에 정의된 뜻과 지금 쓰임이 달라요.
examples.en: The originally defined meaning differs from how it's used now.

examples.ko: 이 단어는 사전에서 어떻게 정의되는지 찾아봤어요.
examples.en: I looked up how this word is defined in the dictionary.
The roles aren't clearly defined, so it's confusing.

explain: 단어, 용어, 문제의 뜻이나 범위가 분명하게 정해질 때 써요. 사람이 하는 '정의하다'와 짝이고 '~로 정의되다'로 어떻게 정해졌는지 말해요. 같은 소리의 '정의'(옳은 것, justice)는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: Used when the meaning or scope of a word, term, or problem is clearly set. It pairs with 정의하다, and you say how with ~로 정의되다. The same-sounding 정의 meaning justice is a different word.

examples.ko: 이 방은 다른 방과 독립돼 있어요.
examples.en: This room is separate from the other rooms.
The department became independent from the company.
If I have a separate space, I study well.
The two systems are independent, so it's safe.
When an organization becomes independent, decisions get faster.
It's hard to work when you aren't independent.

explain: 어떤 것이 다른 것에 묶이지 않고 따로 있다는 뜻이에요. 사람이 부모 집에서 나와 혼자 사는 것은 '독립하다'를 써요. 독립되다는 방, 공간, 조직, 시스템 같은 사물이 주어일 때 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It means something stands apart without being tied to something else. A person moving out and living alone uses 독립하다. 독립되다 fits things like rooms, spaces, organizations, and systems as the subject.

examples.en: The culprit hasn't been identified yet.
The cause has to be pinpointed before it can be fixed.
The time of the accident has been pinned down.
Notifications go only to specified people.
Once the target is identified, I'll contact them right away.
The range is too wide, so it's hard to pin down.

explain: 여러 가능성 중에서 하나로 좁혀져 딱 정해질 때 써요. 뉴스에서 '범인이 특정되다', '원인이 특정되다'처럼 자주 들려요. 명사 앞에 붙는 '특정한'은 '어떤 정해진'이라는 뜻이라 따로 익혀 두세요.
explain_en: Use it when many possibilities narrow down to one that is clearly identified. News often says 범인이 특정되다 or 원인이 특정되다. The form 특정한 before a noun means 'a certain, specific' and is learned separately.

examples.en: The CEO declared that he was starting a new business.
I declare that I'll exercise every day starting this year.
He declared that he's aiming for the championship.

examples.ko: 친구들 앞에서 다이어트를 선언하고 나니 부담돼요.
examples.en: After announcing my diet in front of my friends, I feel the pressure.

examples.ko: 대통령이 새 정책을 선언하는 장면을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the scene of the president announcing a new policy.
It took enough courage to declare independence.

explain: 자기 생각이나 결심을 사람들 앞에서 분명하게 말할 때 써요. '발표하다'는 정해진 내용을 알리는 것이고, 선언하다는 의지와 결심을 크게 밝히는 느낌이에요. 친구끼리 가볍게 '선언한다!'라고도 많이 해요.
explain_en: Use it to state your idea or resolve clearly in front of others. 발표하다 is announcing set information, while 선언하다 stresses declaring your will. Among friends people also say it lightly, like '선언한다!'

en: design; plan out (a structure or system)

examples.en: An architect designed the new library.
We need to design the app again from scratch.

examples.ko: 집을 설계할 때 햇빛을 가장 먼저 생각했어요.
examples.en: When designing the house, I thought about sunlight first.
Take time to plan your future.

examples.ko: 튼튼하게 설계하면 오래 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you design it sturdily, you can use it for a long time.
My younger sibling is designing a robot by himself.

explain: 건물, 기계, 시스템의 구조를 미리 그림이나 계획으로 짜는 일이에요. 겉모양을 꾸미는 '디자인하다'와 달리 구조와 방식을 정하는 쪽이에요. '인생을 설계하다'처럼 계획을 크게 세울 때도 써요.
explain_en: This is planning the structure of a building, machine, or system in advance with drawings or a blueprint. Unlike 디자인하다, which is about appearance, it is about structure and method. It also works for big plans, like 인생을 설계하다.

en: continue; carry on; keep up; sustain

examples.en: I keep up exercising steadily.
It's hard to keep this state up for long.
The company kept offering free shipping this year too.
To keep a relationship going, both people need to try.
The strength to keep at it builds skill.

examples.ko: 할인 행사를 다음 달까지 지속할 거예요.
examples.en: We'll continue the sale until next month.

explain: 어떤 행동이나 상태를 끊지 않고 이어 간다는 뜻이에요. '계속하다'와 비슷하지만 더 격식 있고 오래 이어진다는 느낌이 있어요. 비나 더위가 이어질 때는 보통 '지속되다'를 써요.
explain_en: It means keeping an action or state going without breaking it. Similar to 계속하다 but more formal, with a sense of lasting a long time. When rain or heat simply goes on, 지속되다 is the usual choice.

examples.en: My proposal was approved in the meeting.
That law has to be passed in the National Assembly.
If the document screening is passed, you'll get a call.
We only sell products that have passed inspection.

examples.ko: 계획서가 통과되지 않아서 다시 써야 해요.
examples.en: The plan wasn't approved, so I have to rewrite it.
I'm waiting until my application is approved.

explain: 심사, 검사, 투표 같은 단계를 무사히 넘어 인정받았다는 뜻이에요. 내가 시험에 붙을 때는 '통과하다'나 '합격하다'를 써요. 통과되다는 안건이나 서류처럼 사물이 주어일 때 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It means getting through a review, inspection, or vote and being accepted. When you yourself pass an exam, use 통과하다 or 합격하다. 통과되다 is natural when the subject is a thing like a proposal or document.

examples.en: The guard let the car through.
The committee passed that item.
At the airport you put your bags through the scanner.
The teacher let it slide this time.

examples.ko: 여러 번 필터를 통과시켜서 물을 깨끗하게 해요.
examples.en: We run the water through filters several times to clean it.
They're trying hard to push the bill through quickly.

explain: '통과하다'는 내가 지나가는 것이고, 통과시키다는 다른 사람이나 물건을 지나가게 해 주는 것이에요. 사람이 합격을 허락하거나 안건을 승인할 때도 써요. '~을/를 통과시키다' 틀로 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: 통과하다 is passing through yourself, while 통과시키다 is letting someone or something else pass. It also covers approving a person or an agenda item. The frame is ~을/를 통과시키다.

examples.ko: 이 학교는 백 년 전에 설립됐어요.
examples.en: This school was founded a hundred years ago.
A new company is being established in Seoul.
Once the foundation is established, it will give scholarships.
It's a publishing company founded in 1990.
I covered the process of the institute being established.

examples.ko: 아직 설립되지 않은 단체라서 이름이 없어요.
examples.en: It's an organization not yet established, so it has no name.

explain: 회사, 학교, 단체, 재단처럼 조직을 세워 만드는 일에 써요. 건물을 짓는 것은 '세워지다/지어지다'라서 구분돼요. 회사 소개에서 '○○년에 설립된'이라는 말이 아주 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Used for organizations like companies, schools, groups, and foundations being set up. A building being put up is 세워지다 or 지어지다, so they differ. In company intros, the phrase '○○년에 설립된' appears constantly.

en: continue in succession; be consecutive; be continuous

examples.en: Rainy days keep coming one after another.
Even if failures continue in a row, I won't give up.
Good things kept happening in a row, so I feel great.
This is a stretch where accidents keep happening, so be careful.
If the overtime keeps going day after day, my body gets tired.
Don't use consecutive numbers as a password.

explain: 같은 일이나 상태가 끊기지 않고 줄줄이 이어질 때 써요. '일이 이어지다'보다 횟수가 여러 번이라는 느낌이 있어요. '연속 3일', '3연속'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: Used when the same event or state follows one after another without a break. Compared with 이어지다, it stresses that it happens several times in a row. The noun forms are common too, like 연속 3일 and 3연속.

examples.en: This book is divided into three parts.
They are clothes that are easy to tell apart by color.
The two words are distinguished by how they're used.
The trash is sorted by type.
You can't tell them apart from appearance alone.
Work goes smoothly when public and private are kept separate.

explain: '~으로 구분되다'는 여러 부분으로 나뉘는 것, '~와 구분되다'는 다른 것과 달라서 알아볼 수 있는 것이에요. 비슷한 '구별되다'는 차이를 알아보는 쪽에 더 가까워요. 책이나 목록을 나눌 때는 구분되다를 자주 써요.
explain_en: ~으로 구분되다 means being divided into parts, and ~와 구분되다 means being told apart from something else. 구별되다 leans more toward noticing a difference. For splitting books or lists, 구분되다 is common.

examples.en: This shop's quality is guaranteed.
The safety of personal information must be guaranteed.
There's no method that guarantees you'll pass.
Workers' right to rest is guaranteed.

examples.ko: 성공이 보장되지 않아도 해 볼 거예요.
examples.en: Even if success isn't guaranteed, I'll try.
I want to live in a country where freedom is guaranteed.

explain: 품질, 안전, 권리, 결과 같은 것이 틀림없이 지켜진다는 뜻이에요. 사람이 약속하는 '보장하다'와 짝이고, '보장되다'는 그 약속이 이미 지켜지는 상태예요. 광고에서 '품질 보장'이라는 명사 형태로도 많이 봐요.
explain_en: It means things like quality, safety, rights, or results are surely upheld. It pairs with 보장하다, where a person promises, and 보장되다 is the state of that promise being kept. In ads you often see the noun form, like 품질 보장.
